title: Primary 3 Addition and Subtraction
seo_title: P3 Addition and Subtraction Worksheets: Free Primary 3 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus)
standard_text: Addition and subtraction algorithms (up to 4 digits); mental calculation of two 2-digit numbers
meta_desc: Free P3 maths practice: mental sums, 4-digit addition and subtraction with renaming, checking with the inverse and bar models. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Line up the digits by place value. Rename when you need to.
body_html:
Mental sums with 2-digit numbers

Split one number into tens and ones. Add or take away the tens first, then the ones.

Use a near ten

What is 46 + 29?

29 is 1 less than 30. 46 + 30 = 76. You added 1 too many, so take 1 away: 76 − 1 = 75.

Answer: 75

4-digit addition: rename when a column makes 10 or more

Put ones under ones, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds and thousands under thousands. Start with the ones on the right. If a column makes 10 or more, write the ones digit and rename: 10 ones = 1 ten, 10 tens = 1 hundred, 10 hundreds = 1 thousand.

4-digit subtraction: rename when the top digit is smaller

Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. If the top digit is smaller, rename 1 from the next place as 10.

Across zeros: in 5000 − 1268 there are no hundreds, tens or ones to rename. Rename 1 thousand as 10 hundreds, then 1 hundred as 10 tens, then 1 ten as 10 ones. Each 0 in the middle becomes 9.

Check with the inverse

Addition and subtraction undo each other. To check a subtraction, add the answer to the number you took away. To check an addition, take one number away from the answer.

Check

Is 5000 − 1268 = 3732 right?

Add back: 3732 + 1268 = 5000. You get the number you started with, so it is right.

Answer: Yes

Word problems: draw a bar model

Draw the whole and the parts. Put a ? on the part you need to find. If you know the whole and a part, subtract. If you know all the parts, add.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Not renaming (3467 + 2585 = 5942)Write the renamed 1 in the next column and add it in
Taking the smaller digit from the larger one (6327 − 2854 = 4533)Always take the bottom digit from the top digit. Rename when the top digit is smaller
Making the 0s into 10s (5000 − 1268 = 3842)Only the ones get 10. The 0s in the middle become 9
Lining up the columns wrongly (2456 + 317 = 5626)Line up the ones on the right: 2456 + 317 = 2773

faq.q: What is taught in P3 addition and subtraction?
faq.a: In Primary 3, students add and subtract numbers up to 4 digits with the column method, and add and subtract two 2-digit numbers mentally. They check answers with the inverse and solve word problems with bar models.

faq.q: How do I explain renaming to my child?
faq.a: Renaming means changing 10 of one place for 1 of the next place, such as 10 ones for 1 ten. In subtraction it goes the other way: 1 ten is renamed as 10 ones when the top digit is too small.

faq.q: How do you subtract across zeros, like 5000 − 1268?
faq.a: Rename 1 thousand as 10 hundreds, then 1 hundred as 10 tens, then 1 ten as 10 ones. 5000 becomes 4 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 10 ones, so 5000 − 1268 = 3732.

faq.q: Is this in the MOE syllabus?
faq.a: Yes. Addition and subtraction up to 4 digits and mental calculation with two 2-digit numbers are part of Whole Numbers in the MOE 2021 Primary 3 Mathematics Syllabus (Standard Mathematics).

items.q: 29 is 1 less than 30. What is 46 + 29?

items.e: Take away the tens, then the ones. 91 − 50 = 41. 41 − 8 = 33. (47 takes 1 from 8 instead of 8 from 11.)

items.q: 39 is 1 less than 40. What is 75 − 39?
items.e: Take away 40. You took away 1 too many, so add 1 back. 75 − 40 = 35. 35 + 1 = 36.

items.q: Count on from 67 to 82. What is 82 − 67?
items.e: The numbers are close, so count on. 67 + 3 = 70. 70 + 12 = 82. 3 + 12 = 15.

items.q: What number goes in the box? 45 + ☐ = 92
items.e: Use subtraction: 92 − 45. 92 − 40 = 52. 52 − 5 = 47. Check: 45 + 47 = 92. (137 adds instead of subtracting.)

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ − 28 = 45
items.e: Add back what was taken away: 45 + 28. 45 + 20 = 65. 65 + 8 = 73. Check: 73 − 28 = 45. (17 subtracts instead of adding. 63 forgets that 13 ones is 1 ten and 3 ones.)

items.q: Take away the tens, then the ones. What is 64 − 28?
items.e: 64 − 20 = 44. 44 − 8 = 36. (44 takes 4 from 8 instead of 8 from 14.)

items.q: Arjun has 48 stickers. His friend gives him 37 more. How many stickers does Arjun have now?
items.e: More stickers come in, so add. 48 + 30 = 78. 78 + 7 = 85.

items.q: Hafiz’s storybook has 93 pages. He has read 56 pages. How many pages are left?
items.e: Find what is left, so subtract. 93 − 50 = 43. 43 − 6 = 37. Check: 37 + 56 = 93.

items.q: Find the missing part.
items.e: Whole − part = missing part: 9015 − 4628. Line up the ones. Start on the right. Ones: 5 − 8. Rename 1 ten as 10 ones: 15 − 8 = 7. Tens: 0 − 2. There are 0 hundreds, so rename 1 thousand as 10 hundreds, then 1 hundred as 10 tens. The 0 becomes 9. 10 − 2 = 8. Hundreds: 9 − 6 = 3. Thousands: 8 − 4 = 4. Answer: 4387. Check: 4387 + 4628 = 9015.

items.q: Nurul works out 4005 − 1738 = 2267. Then she checks it by working out 2267 + 1738. What answer should the check give?
items.e: Adding back the number taken away gives the number you started with: 2267 + 1738 = 4005. So 4005 − 1738 = 2267 is correct.

items.q: Kavya works out 3456 + 2789 = 6245. Then she checks it by working out 6245 − 2789. What answer should the check give?
items.e: Taking away one number you added gives the other number: 6245 − 2789 = 3456. So 3456 + 2789 = 6245 is correct.

items.q: 5132 − 2764 = 2368. Which calculation gives 5132?
items.e: Answer + the number taken away = the start number: 2368 + 2764 = 5132.

items.q: Which number sentence is NOT in the same family as 3456 + 2789 = 6245?
items.e: A family uses the same three numbers: 3456, 2789 and 6245. 3456 − 2789 = 667 is true, but 667 is not one of the three numbers.

items.q: On Saturday, 2548 people visited the Singapore Zoo in the morning and 1876 people visited in the afternoon. How many people visited the zoo that day?
items.e: Put the two parts together, so add. 2548 + 1876 = 4424. Check: 4424 − 1876 = 2548.

items.q: A school library had 3465 books. It bought 1287 new books. How many books does the library have now?
items.e: New books are added, so add. 3465 + 1287 = 4752. Check: 4752 − 1287 = 3465.

items.q: At the school fair, the P3 classes raised $1365 and the P4 classes raised $1758. How much money did they raise altogether?
Devi walked 1850 m from her HDB block to the library. Then she walked 1375 m to the hawker centre. How far did she walk altogether?
items.e: Put the two parts of the walk together, so add. 1850 + 1375 = 3225. Check: 3225 − 1375 = 1850.

items.q: A hall has 1500 seats for the Children’s Day concert. 1268 pupils are seated. How many seats are empty?
items.e: Find the part that is left, so subtract. 1500 − 1268 = 232. Check: 232 + 1268 = 1500.

items.q: A bakery made 2400 mooncakes for the Mid-Autumn Festival. It sold 1785 of them. How many mooncakes were left?
items.e: Find what is left, so subtract. 2400 − 1785 = 615. Check: 615 + 1785 = 2400.

items.q: Hui Min’s school has 1835 pupils. Ethan’s school has 2140 pupils. How many more pupils does Ethan’s school have?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. 2140 − 1835 = 305. Check: 305 + 1835 = 2140.

items.q: A shop had 3000 red packets before Chinese New Year. It sold 1746 of them. How many red packets were left?
items.e: Find what is left, so subtract. 3000 − 1746 = 1254. Check: 1254 + 1746 = 3000.

items.q: Mrs Lim wants to buy a laptop that costs $1250. She has saved $875. How much more money does she need?
items.e: Find the difference, so subtract. $1250 − $875 = $375. Check: $375 + $875 = $1250.

items.q: There were some people at East Coast Park in the morning. In the afternoon, 1385 more people came. Then there were 4012 people. How many people were there in the morning?
items.e: Work backwards. Take away the 1385 that came later: 4012 − 1385 = 2627. Check: 2627 + 1385 = 4012.

items.q: A fruit stall had some durians on Saturday morning. It sold 1365 durians and had 1478 left. How many durians did it have at the start?
items.e: Work backwards. Add back the 1365 that were sold: 1478 + 1365 = 2843. Check: 2843 − 1365 = 1478.

items.q: The school aims to collect 6000 cans of food for a charity. P3 pupils collect 1865 cans and P4 pupils collect 2348 cans. How many more cans are needed?
items.e: Step 1, cans collected: 1865 + 2348 = 4213. Step 2, cans still needed: 6000 − 4213 = 1787.

items.q: Mr Rahman had $4500. He paid $1385 for a television and $968 for a washing machine. How much money did he have left?
An MRT train had 1625 passengers. At the next station, 748 passengers got off and 586 passengers got on. How many passengers are on the train now?
items.e: Step 1, after the passengers got off: 1625 − 748 = 877. Step 2, after the new passengers got on: 877 + 586 = 1463.

items.q: On Saturday, 2365 people visited Gardens by the Bay. On Sunday, 1478 more people visited than on Saturday. How many people visited on the two days?
items.e: Step 1, Sunday’s visitors: 2365 + 1478 = 3843. Step 2, both together: 2365 + 3843 = 6208.

items.q: A bubble tea shop sold 1846 cups in June. In July, it sold 379 fewer cups than in June. How many cups did it sell in the two months?
items.e: Step 1, July’s cups: 1846 − 379 = 1467. Step 2, both together: 1846 + 1467 = 3313.

items.q: Ahmad walked 3250 steps in the morning and 4105 steps in the afternoon. How many more steps did he walk in the afternoon?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. 4105 − 3250 = 855. Check: 855 + 3250 = 4105.

items.q: Mdm Wong has 3000 g of flour. She uses 1275 g to bake kueh for Hari Raya Puasa. How much flour is left?
items.e: Find what is left, so subtract. 3000 − 1275 = 1725. Check: 1725 + 1275 = 3000.

items.q: Ethan’s class collected 1485 bottles for recycling. Zhi Hao’s class collected 268 more bottles than Ethan’s class. How many bottles did the two classes collect?
items.e: Step 1, Zhi Hao’s class: 1485 + 268 = 1753. Step 2, both together: 1485 + 1753 = 3238.

items.q: A jug has 1250 ml of water. Wei Ming pours in 975 ml more. How much water is in the jug now?
items.e: More water is poured in, so add. 1250 + 975 = 2225. Check: 2225 − 975 = 1250.
